public_rationale: Public First's August 8–12, 2026 survey of 2,007 U.S. adults, weighted to be nationally representative, found 31% support and 33% opposition to building more AI-training data centers in America [e1]. That substantial supportive minority contradicts essentially absent public appetite [e1]. A separate question found 26% support and 46% opposition to a generic data center in respondents' communities, showing greater local opposition alongside substantial support [e1].
limitations: The survey was published on August 26, after the August 21 post, but its fieldwork falls within the assessment window [e1].
The local question concerns generic data centers; it does not directly measure support for nearby AI-specific construction [e1].
These polling results do not assess the separate claim about data-center economics.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is essentially no public appetite for the AI data center buildout.

statement.excerpt: Nobody wants this, and the economics make no sense.

from_speaker: Part II: public opinion, refracted through politics
our_interpretation: Assess the supplied proposition about public appetite, not the separate judgment that the economics make no sense.
The US political context identifies the relevant public as Americans.
The plain reading is essentially absent public support, allowing ordinary rhetorical exaggeration. It is stronger than saying opponents outnumber supporters.

Use August 1–21, 2026, the current month through publication, for an ongoing public-opinion state that surveys could measure before the post. Earlier polling is background; later publication of pre-post fieldwork is admissible.
criteria.support_condition: Representative polling finds negligible support for AI data-center construction, with the result robust to ordinary differences between national and local questions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative polling finds a substantial supportive minority for AI data-center construction, even if opposition is greater.
